0.5.2 fixes how the viewer protects pages that it cannot prepare, whose links it could not see, or
that run scripts, a refresh that could overwrite another HTML file, and smaller defects in links and
find. This personal
fork supports Linux desktop. macOS and mobile are out of scope, and this release is marked
desktop-only. Windows supplies additional development checks. The fork is not in Obsidian's
community plugin directory; install it by hand.

## Install

1. Download `viell-html-page-viewer-0.5.2.zip` below.
2. Unzip it into your vault's `.obsidian/plugins/` folder, so that
   `.obsidian/plugins/viell-html-page-viewer/` holds `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css`,
   replacing those of an earlier version.
3. In Obsidian, open **Settings → Community plugins**. If upstream's **HTML Page Viewer** is
   installed, turn it off: both plugins open `.html` and `.htm` files. Then turn on **HTML Page
   Viewer (viell)**, or turn it off and on again if it was on; if it is not listed yet, reload the
   list of installed plugins.

To go back, install 0.5.1 the same way. Settings are kept. The plugin never changes your notes or
pages.

## Fixed

- **Security:** a page that the viewer cannot prepare for display shows an error, with **Refresh
  preview** and the source view still available, instead of being shown without its protections.
  Escapes in a page's CSS decode as CSS specifies, and a stylesheet that cannot be read is left
  out, as a missing one is.
- **Security:** links inside a page's shadow DOM, which pages saved with their web components can
  contain, open in Obsidian as other links do, and the page stays in its frame. After a tab moves
  to another tab group or window, its page follows links in Obsidian as soon as it shows again;
  before, a link clicked before the page had loaded again navigated the frame away from the page.
- **Security:** with scripts on, a page's frame is isolated from the vault's files from the moment
  it is created. On some Obsidian versions, such as 1.5.3, such a page could, rarely, load vault
  files that it names, such as its images, without the **Local files with scripts on** setting.
- A refresh that finishes after another file has opened in the same tab no longer shows the earlier
  file's contents there. Before, Obsidian then saved those contents over the file that the tab
  showed once the tab moved on; the viewer no longer lets Obsidian save the files it shows.
- Links in SVG drawn in the page open as other links do. A link to `#` scrolls to the top of the
  page, and a link to `#top` goes to the element named `top` when the page has one.
- Find in the page leaves out text that CSS hides, and closing the find bar keeps a query typed
  just before it closed.
- **Rendered**, **Source**, and **Split** form a labelled group, and the selected one says it is
  pressed, so that screen readers announce which view mode a tab shows.

## Known limits

- With scripts on, the find bar searches only the source, split-view scrolling is independent,
  and links work as in a browser frame. Local files load only with **Local files with scripts
  on**, within its 8 MB per-file and 32 MB per-page limits. Files loaded by scripts themselves,
  imported modules, and pages in frames do not load.
- Stylesheets from the web do not apply, apart from Google Fonts. Local stylesheets must end in
  `.css`.
- A link to a part of another page opens that page at its top. A link that SVG `<use>` copies from
  elsewhere in the page does nothing when clicked.
- Find in the page still counts some text that Obsidian never paints, and leaves out a closed
  select's chosen option ([#122](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/122)).
  Content inside shadow DOM, which some saved pages contain, is not searched, gets no tooltips, and
  is not prepared like the rest of the page
  ([#124](https://github.com/viell-dev/slop-html-page-viewer/issues/124)).

## Testing

Tested in Linux Obsidian 1.5.3 and 1.15.1: page rendering, the page's protections and their error
state, links, find, split view, settings, refreshing and leaving a tab without writing any file,
installing this release's zip, turning the plugin off and on, updating it, and restarting Obsidian,
and the synthetic archive corpus compared with the frozen prototype. Build and unit checks also run
on Windows. `SHA256SUMS` lists the checksums of the files below.
